scope: Mutable supplied accessor gain over immutable interleaved stereo Float32 or exact decoded PCM24, fixed supplied rates, retained mode1/mode2 state and bounded equal-rate fast-path arithmetic. This is a development/core review, not packaged GUI acceptance or proof of the hosted backend or gain owner.

review_findings.detail: Both native fast-path prefixes reject unequal rates. The admitted Float32-destination generic up path is type conversion then gain then filtering; the down path is source-format filtering, conditional packed24 roundtrip, type conversion and gain. Current Swift preserves these orders, with no sample clipping in the destination Float32 multiply.

For signed zero or finite |gain|>=2^-95, gain*2^-31 and gain*2^-23 stay normal and exact. Signed24 and signed24<<8 are exactly representable. Both native decoder paths and exact decoded-Float32 followed by gain present the same exact product to one Float32 rounding. The app rejects lower nonzero equal-PCM24 gains;709 independently derived below-bound cases discriminate the alternatives.

Native setter100370538 writes gain only; each conversion read copies it into retained converter state. Gain!=1 consumes first-conversion state even at equal Float32 rates. Swift setGain leaves cursor/first/filter untouched, including rejected-setter controls; existing seek also preserves history. Upsampling zero-gain calls can return prior nonzero filtered history, while downsampling gains the current returned buffer.

The C gain helper validates all samples/results and the arm64 FP environment before writing. Signed zeros are preserved, unity copies, no clipping. Invalid gain, subnormal input/result, nonfinite/overflow and non-nearest tests reject without changing buffers. A processing failure poisons Swift state because the retained backend might already have advanced. Postterminal gain edits remain explicitly excluded by the application.

validation.instruction_count_scope: Retained disassembly rows, possibly overlapping; not unique address coverage.
validation.standalone_author_controls: Inspected sealed optimized and UBSan reports,117593 assertions and7 FP rejections per build; not rerun by this reviewer.
validation.full_suite: Parent-owned separate run, not claimed by this focused review.

limits: Expected gain arithmetic uses Fraction/integer IEEE rounding and no candidate implementation. Mode1 oracle retains the shared host-libm sin/sqrt limitation; mode2 wrapper comparison uses the same pinned public SoXR backend, not the unknown vendor build.
Source format, accessor gain and source/output rates are explicit supplied context. Saved WAV metadata or project rate does not prove the selected native backend, rate or gain owner.
The equal-PCM24 bound, finite normal-or-zero policy, transactional errors, poisoned-state handling and postterminal exclusion are application boundaries, not native rejection claims.
The native scalar/SIMD choice below the admitted equal-PCM24 bound, other formats/layouts, dynamic rate change and full generic converter behavior are not implemented here.

Event/segment gain stays a separate owner. Existing audition stream gain placement is not reclassified by this accessor contract, and production timeline use does not automatically select this nonunity accessor path.
No proprietary target execution, Cubase export/sample comparison, hosted scheduler comparison, device capture or full-application fidelity claim.
